record.paper_title: Open problems in the Kontsevich graph construction of Poisson bracket symmetries
record.original_question: What are the Liouville-integrability and possible super-integrability properties of the nonlinear evolutionary PDE systems Ṗ = Q(P) that arise from known Kontsevich graph symmetries of Poisson bi-vectors?

evidence.quote: Problem 9. What are the (Liouville, in particular super-)integrability properties of these nonlinear evolutionary PDE systems P˙ = Q(P) ?

artifact.category_tag: Kontsevich graph flows on Poisson structures
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. Let $M$ be a smooth (or formal) manifold and let $P=P^{ij}(x)\,\partial_i\wedge\partial_j$ be a Poisson bi-vector on $M$, i.e. a smooth section of $\Lambda^2 TM$ satisfying the Jacobi identity $[\![P,P]\!]=0$, where $[\![\cdot,\cdot]\!]$ denotes the Schouten–Nijenhuis bracket. A Kontsevich graph cocycle is a finite linear combination $\gamma=\sum c_\alpha \Gamma_\alpha$ of oriented graphs $\Gamma_\alpha$ on $n$ internal (aerial) vertices and two ground (sink) vertices, with two outgoing edges from each internal vertex, such that the universal bi-vector $Q_\gamma(P)$ obtained by inserting copies of $P$ at the internal vertices and contracting along the edge orientations satisfies the infinitesimal-symmetry equation
$$[\![P,Q_\gamma(P)]\!]=0\qquad\text{for every Poisson bi-vector }P.$$
Such a $\gamma$ thus determines a flow $\dot P = Q_\gamma(P)$ on the variety of Poisson structures, where the right-hand side is a polynomial differential expression in the components $P^{ij}$ and their partial derivatives. Concrete examples include the tetrahedral flow $\dot P = Q_{\gamma_3}(P)$ and the higher graph cocycles $\gamma_5,\gamma_7,\dots$ producing nonlinear evolutionary PDE systems for the components $P^{ij}(x,t)$.

Recall that an evolutionary PDE system is called Liouville-integrable if it admits an infinite hierarchy of independent commuting symmetries (equivalently, an infinite family of Poisson-commuting conserved functionals in involution with respect to a compatible Hamiltonian structure), and super-integrable if it admits, in addition, further independent (not necessarily commuting) integrals beyond what Liouville integrability requires.

Problem. Determine the Liouville-integrability and, when applicable, the super-integrability properties of the nonlinear evolutionary PDE systems $\dot P = Q_\gamma(P)$ associated with the known Kontsevich graph symmetries $\gamma$ of Poisson bi-vectors (in particular $\gamma_3$, $\gamma_5$, $\gamma_7$, and the linear combinations of graph cocycles producing nontrivial Poisson cohomology classes). Specifically:
(a) Exhibit, or prove the nonexistence of, an infinite hierarchy of commuting symmetries of $\dot P = Q_\gamma(P)$.
(b) Construct a (bi-)Hamiltonian formulation, recursion operator, or Lax representation, or prove that none exists.
(c) Decide whether any such system is super-integrable in the sense above.
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution of the integrability question for the evolutionary PDE flows $\dot P = Q_\gamma(P)$ generated by Kontsevich graph cocycles (tetrahedral $\gamma_3$, pentagon-wheel $\gamma_5$, etc.) was found. The question is posed as an open problem in the literature on Kontsevich graph symmetries of Poisson structures, and subsequent work by Buring, Kiselev and collaborators has computed examples and verified the symmetry property but not established Liouville- or super-integrability of the resulting flows.
